name: Starter: Belarusian
about: Belarusian in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Belarusian order.

words.у: in, at, on; to (ў after a vowel)
words.быць: be, exist (ёсць: there is, there are; будзе: will be)
words.вы: you (to a stranger, or more than one)
words.холадна: cold (of the weather, or how you feel)

kali-laska.about: Literally if (you'd be) kind; the same to anyone.

concept.line: A person or thing a verb acts on directly often takes the accusative, which turns feminine -а into -у (кава → Я п'ю каву: I drink coffee); so does where you're going after у or на: у краму (to the store), на працу (to work).
Belarusian usually leaves out am, is and are in the present: Я з Амерыкі (I from America), Дзе мае ключы?
A noun with a singular form is masculine, feminine or neuter, mostly told by its ending, and my, your, describing words and the past match it: мой брат, мая сястра, маё акно.
A yes-or-no question often keeps a statement's order with the voice rising (Ты гаворыш па-англійску?), or starts with ці; a question word often comes first: Дзе вакзал?
The verb's ending changes with who does it: я раблю, ты робіш, ён робіць, мы робім, яны робяць.

words.means: жыву = live; жывеш = live; жыве = lives
іду = am going; ідзеш = are going; ідзе = goes

concept.line: Having is usually said as at me there is: У мяне ёсць брат (at me is brother: I have a brother), У нас ёсць вялікая кухня (we have a big kitchen).
